# 0003. Use payment webhooks with an hourly reconciliation poll

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-11-27
- **Supersedes:** [0002. Poll the payment provider for status](0002-poll-payment-status.md)

## Context

Record 0002 chose to poll the provider's status endpoint every 30 seconds
because the provider offered no webhooks in April 2026. That has changed,
according to the team discussion on 2026-11-18 (Ana, payments; Ben, platform;
Chloe, support):

- The provider launched signed webhooks on 2026-11-01. Each event carries an
  HMAC-SHA256 signature over the body, and the same event can arrive more
  than once.
- Polling costs 1.9 million provider calls a month. From 2027-01-01 the
  provider will charge for status calls over 1 million a month.
- Support reports that customers see paid orders as pending for up to
  30 seconds.

## Options considered

- **Keep polling every 30 seconds.** No new endpoint to run. Keeps the
  30-second delay, and at 1.9 million calls a month we would pay for the
  calls over 1 million from 2027-01-01.
- **Switch to webhooks only.** Status updates as the provider sends them,
  and almost no status calls. Needs a public HTTPS endpoint, signature
  checks, and idempotent handling. A missed event would leave an order's
  status wrong, with nothing to correct it.
- **Webhooks plus an hourly reconciliation poll.** The same work and
  benefits as webhooks only, and the slow poll catches missed events, at
  the cost of a small number of status calls and a second code path.

## Decision

Receive payment status updates from the provider's webhooks, and poll the
status endpoint once an hour to reconcile any events that were missed.
Stop the 30-second poll.

- Expose a public HTTPS endpoint for the provider's webhook events.
- Reject any event whose HMAC-SHA256 signature over the body does not
  verify.
- Handle events idempotently, so a repeated event does not change an
  order twice.

## Consequences

- Easier: paid orders show as paid without waiting for the next poll, and
  an hourly poll makes far fewer status calls than one every 30 seconds,
  which matters once calls over 1 million a month are charged from
  2027-01-01.
- Harder: the webhook endpoint is a new public service the team must
  monitor and secure, and status now arrives by two paths that must agree.
- Rules out: running without a publicly reachable endpoint, which 0002
  relied on.
- Revisit if the provider changes how it delivers or signs webhook events,
  or changes its pricing for status calls.
# 0002. Poll the payment provider for status

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-04-11

## Context

The payment provider offered no webhooks in April 2026.

## Options considered

- Poll every 30 seconds.
- Ask customers to refresh.

## Decision

Poll the provider's status endpoint every 30 seconds for open orders.

## Consequences

Easier: no public endpoint. Harder: up to 30 seconds of delay, and 2,880 calls a day per open order. Revisit when the provider offers webhooks.
